messages.subject: Error: Incorrect outcome specification.
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I have a question regarding the truthTable command in R.
I get the message Error: Incorrect outcome specification. I do not know what that means as all conditions are calibrated. The problem continues even when I create a new dataframe with the calibrated variables (+ outcome) only.

I have previously stumbled upon this error message but was able to solve it by either creating a new dataframe or by creating a new csv file with the relevant variables only.

I'm thankful for any advice on this issue.

Best,
Luc

the code for this is:

messages.subject: Re: [QCA] Error: Incorrect outcome specification.
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adrian,

not sure why but it does work now.

I created a new dataframe with the calibrated variables only: test <- panel_QCA[, c ("GRITC", "IQ", "FRIENDS", "MATEDU", "SATISF", "FRANCS")]

Then this code works: truthTable(test, outcome = "GRITC", conditions = "IQ, FRIENDS, MATEDU, SATISF, FRANCS", incl.cut = 0.9, pri.cut = 0.7, complete = TRUE, show.cases = TRUE, sort.by <http://sort.by> = "out")

However, the previous dataframe still doesn't work:  truthTable(panel_QCA, outcome = "GRITC", conditions = "IQ, FRIENDS, MATEDU, SATISF, FRANCS", incl.cut = 0.9, pri.cut = 0.7, complete = TRUE, show.cases = TRUE, sort.by <http://sort.by> = "out")

Anyways, many thanks for your help!

Best,
Luc

messages.subject: Re: [QCA] Error: Incorrect outcome specification.
messages.body_plain:
I am not sure, but what is the first column titled "X" in panel_QCA? If this has not been created by you, I assume it is empty and has been created by R when importing the data (I think it is empty, but if not there is something else weird about it). When I remember correctly this causes problems with some functions. If you want to get to the bottom of it, you could only remove X from panel_QCA and check whether truthTable() works then. In general, I recommend to remove X right after importing the data or use another package/function for data import.

Hi together,

everytime I'm trying to run the suberSubset() on the MreInput file (see below) the calculation takes a lot of time until R is running into the following error: R session aborted. R encoutered a fatal error. The session was terminated.

I am loading the file into R > load into the QCA enviroment > convert it into a data frame > and apply:
superSubset(MreInput, outcome = "Outcome", incl.cut = 0.9, ron.cut = 0.6)
or
superSubset(MreInput, outcome = "Outcome")
> the result is always the same

I hope anybody could help me with that problem, thanks in advance!

Joël

messages.body_plain:
QCA is usually known as a "medium-N" analysis, and that is also related to the number of conditions because there has to be at least a certain number of cases for any given number of conditions (I really hope there are not just 4 cases for 19 conditions).

Having so many potential causes for your outcome will necessarily create millions of potential inter-relations between all of those causes.
And having millions of explanations for a phenomenon is essentially similar to having no explanation at all. Saying "everything goes" is in no way better than saying "I have no explanation".

I counted no less than 19 conditions, that is a whole lot.
Any particular reason why you would need so many conditions?

Best,
Adrian
